what: BCE is Canada's largest telecom company. Through Bell it sells mobile, internet and television service, and it owns media assets including CTV and sports networks.
customers: Canadian households and businesses buying mobile, internet and television service, plus advertisers.
money: mobile, internet, television and business services
television networks, radio and digital advertising
moat: Fibre and mobile networks across Canada in a market with only three large operators, where building a competing network is prohibitively expensive.
risks: Debt of about $29 billion against almost no cash
It cut its dividend in 2025 after years of paying out more than it earned
Canadian wireless price competition has intensified since regulators pushed for lower prices
Media advertising revenue is in structural decline
opportunities: Operating margin of 39% with a dividend yield above 5% even after the cut
Fibre coverage across most of its territory reduces future capital spending
Analysts see about 23% upside from current levels
watch: Mobile revenue per user and free cash flow against the dividend.
